theCountingProblem:
A RESTAURANT WITH A GOOD WINE LIST IS NOT A WINE BAR, AND THE ONLY JUDGED AWARD IN THIS TOPIC IS AN AWARD FOR WINE LISTS.

Star Wine List of the Year UK 2026 gave eleven Gold Stars. Here is what they went to:
  Doppo (Tuscan restaurant, Soho) - Best Long List
  Trivet (two-star restaurant, Bermondsey) - Best Medium-Sized List
  DakaDaka (Georgian restaurant, Heddon St) - Best Short List
  Row on 5 (restaurant, Savile Row) - Best By-the-Glass List
  Labombe by Trivet (restaurant, Old Park Lane) - Best Newcomer List
  Restaurant St. Barts - Sustainability Prize
  Newcomer Wines (Austrian wine bar and shop, Dalston) - Best Austrian List
  Saint Augustine Villa, VENTNOR, ISLE OF WIGHT - Best Rose List
  Mountain (restaurant, Soho) - Best Spanish List
  Claridge's Restaurant (hotel dining room) - Best Riesling List

ONE of those is a wine bar. One is not in London (trap 12: the award is UK-wide and must be scoped before a single citation is counted). Recording this award whole would hand a wine bar guide a Michelin-starred restaurant in Bermondsey and a villa on the Isle of Wight as its top-cited venues.

THE TEST, three questions, TWO OF THREE to be counted:
  1. IS IT NAMED FOR ITS WINE? The name, or the venue's own words - 'wine bar', 'bar a vin', 'cave a manger', 'wine shop and bar'. Self-description wins, the same rule french.json uses for cuisine boundaries.
  2. DOES IT SELL BY THE GLASS AT RANGE? A real by-the-glass list - preservation, Coravin, keg - not four house pours. 28-50 keeps 30+ open; that is range. A restaurant with six is not.
  3. IS DRINKING WITHOUT EATING NORMAL THERE? Can you walk in, take a stool, drink two glasses and leave without ordering food. This is the question that separates a wine bar from a wine-led restaurant, and it is the one readers actually care about.

VERIFIED BORDERLINE CASES ALREADY IN THE SOURCES. Star Wine List's own London 42 includes four PUBS - Canton Arms, Anchor & Hope, Marksman, The Bull & Last. All pass tests 2 and 3, all fail test 1. They are pubs with serious wine, and a guide that counts them is a guide about something else. Decide once, apply to all four, and record the decision here.

TRAP 13 - VENUES ALREADY RECORDED IN OTHER CORPORA. Grep before adding any of these; several already carry counts under another topic and those counts must not be reprinted here:
  british.json    - Noble Rot, 40 Maltby Street, Camille, Luca, Trullo, Akub
  french.json     - Camille, The 10 Cases, Josephine
  italian.json    - Bar Crispin, Luca, Trullo, Enoteca Turi
  spanish.json    - Barrafina (Dean Street and Coal Drops Yard branches)
  bars.json       - 107 Wine Shop & Bar, Peckham Cellars, plus the whole bars-wine scope
  breakfast-brunch.json - Peckham Cellars

Camille, Luca and Trullo are the sharp ones: all three are restaurants that appear on wine bar lists. Run the three-question test on each and write the answer into openVenueQuestions rather than deciding silently.

formatSection.title: Shop price plus corkage
formatSection.note:
THE SECTION NOBODY ELSE PRINTS, AND THE ONE THAT ACTUALLY DECIDES WHERE THE EVENING HAPPENS. A large and growing share of London's best wine bars are bottle shops with stools: you buy the bottle at RETAIL and pay a flat corkage to drink it there. The same bottle that is £45 on a restaurant list is £22 plus a corkage fee in a shop. Not one source found in this pass prints that fee.

THE DRINK-IN FACT IS VERIFIED AND THE SECTION CAN BE BUILT ON IT. Every venue below is described as a bottle-shop hybrid by Star Wine List or by the venue itself:
  Dan's, Dalston - 'bottles offered at retail prices as well as for consuming on site' (Star Wine List)
  Half Cut Market, York Way - 'wine available for take away any time we're open', 'around 80 bottles available for takeaway at any time', selection curated by co-owner Holly Willcocks (halfcut.world, read 2026-09-07)
  Little Cellars, Camberwell - 'next door they have their shop for take away, Cellar Next Door' (Star Wine List)
  Lower, Lower Marsh - 'a cellar shop if you need to pick up a bottle to drink in or take away' (Star Wine List)
  Peckham Cellars - 'to be taken away or drunk in' (Star Wine List)
  Also to check: Quality Wines, Bottle & Rye, Top Cuvee, Stable Wines, 107 Wine Shop & Bar, Veraison, Newcomer Wines, Bedales of Borough, Dynamic Vines, The Winemakers Club

THE CORKAGE NUMBER IS NOT AVAILABLE TO THE FETCHER, AND THIS IS THE ONE THING TO SETTLE BEFORE WRITING THE SECTION. Checked 2026-09-07: qualitywines.co.uk 403s, peckhamcellars.co.uk does not resolve, topcuvee.com is JS-rendered and returns nothing to curl, and halfcut.world confirms take-away but publishes no fee. Coravin, which would be the obvious place for it, carries no prices at all. So the figure has to come from a browser read of each shop's menu page, or from asking.

NEVER INVENT OR ESTIMATE A CORKAGE FIGURE. A wrong number here costs the reader money at the till, which is the same class of error as a dead booking link. Where the fee cannot be confirmed, print the fact that you can drink in and buy at shop prices WITHOUT a number, rather than guessing - and per the standing rule, ASK rather than publishing the gap.

WHY NOT THE OTHER CANDIDATES. By-the-glass and Coravin pricing is real and is carried as a facet value instead, but it splits venues badly - almost everywhere pours by the glass, and the prices are as unpublished as corkage. Walk-in versus booking is the standard booking summary every guide on this site already runs near the top, not a section of its own. Shop-price-plus-corkage is the only candidate that is both a hard fact and a decision the reader actually makes.
